=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1037-1068 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: compare_against_baseline still treats `baseline_satisfied is None` with `check_error` as a new violation instead of pre-existing drift.
  WHY: The compare-mode branch only exempts `baseline_satisfied is False`, so fingerprints absent from the baseline can still hard-fail and recreate the retry loop.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:429-1204 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_restore_attempt_base` does not restore `RESOLVER_FP_BASELINE_STATE_FILE` between retries.
  WHY: The retry restore path only copies allowlisted repo files, so the captured baseline can be lost or go stale and later retries can fall back to absolute verification.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1040-1069 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The must_contain ratio warning counts pre-existing drift in the denominator, so compare mode emits a misleading Silent-regression detector warning on pure-drift passes.
  WHY: `mc_total_expected` includes current must_contain fingerprints that were already failing at baseline, so the warning can fire even when the run ultimately passes with pre-existing drift.
- tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline.py:252-294 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new compare-mode test only covers a single-issue pre-existing check_error case.
  WHY: Mixed runs with one pre-existing drift and one genuine regression remain untested, so per-issue iteration/state-leak bugs could slip through.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1037-1072 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: There is no compare-mode test coverage for `must_not_exist` classification.
  WHY: `must_not_exist` uses a different key shape and shared drift-marker path, so a regression there could hard-fail or silently pass without detection.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~1068 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In compare mode, `_emit_must_contain_ratio` fires the "Silent-regression detector" warning whenever `mc_total_satisfied < mc_total_expected`.
  WHY: When all unsatisfied must_contain fingerprints are pre-existing drift, the warning text "Investigating violations below" is misleading because the violations list is empty and the run passes with pre-existing drift markers.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1047-1053 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `compare_against_baseline` treats missing baseline entries with `check_error` as violations instead of pre-existing drift.
  WHY: When `baseline_satisfied` is `None` and `state["check_error"]` is not `None`, the code adds to `violations`, which incorrectly fails the resolver on fingerprints that may have had issues before the resolver ran.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1040-1045 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The must_contain ratio warning includes pre-existing drift fingerprints in the denominator.
  WHY: `mc_total_expected` counts all current must_contain patterns regardless of whether they are pre-existing drift, causing the silent-regression warning to fire even when all failures are already-known issues.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:465-490 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_restore_attempt_base` does not restore `RESOLVER_FP_BASELINE_STATE_FILE` between retries.
  WHY: Subsequent retries can lose the baseline state and fall back to absolute verification, losing the pre-existing drift exemption.
- tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline.py:254-290 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test only covers single-issue fingerprint entries with `check_error`.
  WHY: It does not cover mixed scenarios where one issue has pre-existing drift while another issue in the same run has a genuine resolver-introduced regression.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
(No findings reported.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1037-1068 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `state["check_error"] is not None` and `baseline_satisfied is None`, `compare_against_baseline` falls through to `violations.append(state["violation"])`.
  WHY: A fingerprint that was unreadable in both baseline and current will still hard-fail instead of being treated as pre-existing drift, recreating the resolver loop for files that were never accessible.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:429-460 and 1190-1204 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `RESOLVER_FP_BASELINE_STATE_FILE` is captured once before the retry loop but is never restored by `_restore_attempt_base`.
  WHY: After retries restore the working tree, the baseline file can be stale or missing, causing the verifier to fall back to absolute mode and lose the pre-existing-drift exemption.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1061-1068 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `_emit_must_contain_ratio` call uses `mc_total_expected`, which counts all current must_contain fingerprints including pre-existing drift.
  WHY: The "Silent-regression detector" warning appears in logs even when compare mode passes because the drift is pre-existing.
- tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline.py:252-294 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new test only exercises a single-issue fingerprint entry.
  WHY: It does not test the mixed case where one issue has pre-existing drift while another issue has a genuine resolver-introduced regression in the same run.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1061-1068 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The must_contain ratio counts every current fingerprint in `mc_total_expected`, including those that are pre-existing drift.
  WHY: When a run has only pre-existing failures, `_emit_must_contain_ratio` fires the "Silent-regression detector" warning even though compare mode will ultimately pass with "PASSED with pre-existing drift".
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1037-1072 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: There is no test coverage for `must_not_exist` compare-mode classification.
  WHY: `must_not_exist` uses a different fp_key shape and the shared drift-marker code path, so a bug in baseline index construction or marker emission for this kind would go undetected.
- tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline.py:255-293 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new test exercises a single-issue fingerprint where the only pattern has a pre-existing check error.
  WHY: It does not verify compare mode with one pre-existing check error and a second genuine resolver-introduced regression in the same run.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~1043 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After the baseline-satisfied lookup was reordered, a pre-existing check_error can still reach the violations path in mixed-issue cases.
  WHY: The `baseline_satisfied is False` guard does not fully cover the `None` case, so an already-broken fingerprint can still be treated as a new regression and recreate the perpetual loop.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~1069 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ratio warning still counts total captured must_contain, including pre-existing drift items.
  WHY: It fires even on pure-drift-pass runs, which produces spurious Silent-regression detector noise in logs and audit tooling.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:~429-460 and ~1190-1204 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The baseline state file is captured once before the retry loop but is never restored by `_restore_attempt_base`.
  WHY: A timeout or validation failure on retry #2+ can leave the baseline missing, causing fallback to absolute verification and losing the pre-existing-drift exemption.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
